answer: Marble-Weighted Capacity Lottery. Each identity must post a small non-refundable compute deposit to enter a queue; admission is granted probabilistically, proportional to deposit, at a fixed global rate. When demand peaks, the queue swells like an ocean and a cloned identity’s expected service value stays flat while its deposit is forfeited on rejection. An onyx token marks confirmed admission and expires, forcing re-entry. Clones therefore face strictly negative marginal EV: every extra identity adds a sunk deposit with no throughput gain.
